chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Those who remember Allah while standing and sitting' (1), he said: 'The healthy person prays standing and sitting; the sick person prays sitting; and on their sides [prays] the one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting.'

key_terms.الصَّحِيحُ: The healthy person (one with full capability)
key_terms.الْمَرِيضُ: The sick person (one with reduced capability)

ai.seo_question: What are the different postures for prayer based on a person's health and strength?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* elucidates the graduated flexibility in prayer postures (*ahwal al-salah*) according to physical capacity, linking the Quranic verse 3:191 to practical jurisprudence. It establishes a hierarchy where the healthy prays standing (with sitting as valid), the sick prays sitting, and the severely weak prays lying on their side, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (*taysir*) in worship. This interpretation underscores the Prophetic tradition of adapting ritual obligations to individual circumstances without compromising the essence of prayer.
